speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you tell me exactly when the rash first appeared and how it has changed since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the facial rash have a "slapped cheek" appearance, and is the rash on her extremities lacy or net-like? I also need to know if she has been exposed to anyone with a similar illness recently.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area is highly suggestive of a "slapped cheek" appearance. Given the preceding viral symptoms and the lacy nature of the body rash, this presentation is classic for Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)
